page: Amazon Web Services c9gd.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 64-bit Arm-based AWS Graviton processors. It features 4 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz with a single thread per core and no hyperthreading. Memory capacity is provisioned at 8.0 GB, delivering a 2.0 GB per core ratio aligned with compute-focused execution profiles.

Local ephemeral storage is bundled directly with the hardware, consisting of a 237 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume designed for low-latency scratch operations. Network performance is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps managed through Nitro offload cards. The platform does not incorporate discrete GPU accelerators.

The 1:2 memory-to-core configuration makes the c9gd.xlarge cost-efficient for processor-bound tasks where large RAM arrays are unnecessary. Its local NVMe storage provides rapid I/O for temporary files, making it suitable for distributed build jobs, CI/CD runners, batch processing, log ingestion, and stateless web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services c9gd.xlarge is a compute-optimized Nitro-based virtual server powered by custom 64-bit Arm AWS Graviton processors. Configured with 4 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz with 1 thread per core, the system provides 8.0 GB of memory, yielding a compute-aligned 2.0 GB per core allocation. A key feature is its bundled 237 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume, which provides high-speed, direct-attached ephemeral storage alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not feature GPU acceleration. Thanks to its dedicated physical Arm cores, targeted memory footprint, and low-latency NVMe scratch capacity, the c9gd.xlarge delivers cost-efficient performance for compute-heavy workloads requiring fast local storage, such as CI/CD build environments, batch data processing, web serving, and media encoding pipelines.
